chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

"If a man resolves to stay for ten days, he must complete the prayer. And if he is in doubt, not knowing how long he will stay, saying 'today or tomorrow,' he must shorten [the prayer] for the period between him and a month. If he stays in that city for more than a month, he must complete the prayer."

And whenever a person sets out for travel after dawn, if he had intended the travel during the night, fasting is incumbent upon him [to break it]. And if he did not intend it during the night, fasting that day becomes obligatory upon him. And if he set out before the rising of dawn, breaking the fast is also obligatory upon him, even if he had not intended the travel during the night.
And that which indicates what we have mentioned is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a traveler's prayer and fasting if they decide to travel after dawn?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational criteria for the traveler's prayer (Salat al-Musafir) and fasting rules, specifically addressing the ambiguity of the 'ten-day' threshold and the impact of intention (niyyah) on fasting validity. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on distinguishing between temporary travel and prolonged residence, a key distinction in the school of Ahl al-Bayt. The hadith also clarifies the specific scenario of departing after dawn, linking the obligation to fast directly to whether the intention to travel was formed before or after the Fajr prayer.
